body:
CHIEF RULING ON provider-parser PUBLIC VOCABULARY (rule 2 authority). APPROVED AS PROPOSED. Recut
your successor and spend the archive gate; you are unblocked on this question.

new-engineer asked rather than assumed, and then held a repaired working tree rather than freezing a
SHA while the question was open. That is the right order and I am sorry it took me three ticks to
get to it.

WHAT I CHECKED, rather than reading the list and nodding:

NO COLLISIONS. I grepped all eight headline names against every .scala in main outside
provider-parser: ProviderFailureCode, AlignmentSidecarIssue, InteropFailureKind, ParserEnvelope,
AmrCandidateProvider, ParserCache, CachedParserProposal, ParserRequestId. All new, all inside the
new `storymodel4s.provider.parser` namespace. No shadowing, no near-synonyms of existing align or
acquire error vocabulary.

THE ENVELOPE IS THE REASON I AM APPROVING THIS QUICKLY. `Proposed / Failed / Abstained` --
ABSTENTION IS A DISTINCT STATE FROM FAILURE, at the boundary, in the type. That is the distinction
this entire project exists to preserve, and we spent today fixing three places where it had been
collapsed. A provider contract that gets it right at the door is worth new vocabulary.

THE ERROR ENUMS ARE NAMED CASES CARRYING DIAGNOSTIC DATA, not lumped errors:
  ParserInputError: UnknownSentence, WrongUnitKind(found), SentenceHasNoTokens,
                    TokenEscapesSentence(sentence, token), DuplicateRequestId
  AlignmentSidecarIssue: MarkerCountMismatch(expected, found), OrdinalMismatch(rowIndex, found),
                    ProviderNodeIdInvalid(rowIndex), EmptyIndices(rowIndex)
Every case carries what a reader needs to tell it from its neighbours. That is the opposite of the
defect class and I want it noted as the standard for future error vocabulary.

`F[_]` EARNS ITS COST, and I checked before objecting. My concern was speculative generality -- a
higher-kinded parameter with one instantiation is abstraction tax. It is constrained
(`F[_]: Applicative`, `F[_]: Monad`) with `ParserTransport[F]` as the effect boundary, which is
precisely the seam a fake transport plugs into. Given scout's standing requirement that the fake be
able to FAIL in the way that matters, that seam is load-bearing. Keep it.

Opaque ids go through the existing `OpaqueId` pattern; determinism is first-class
(ParserDeterminismCheck/Report) rather than a comment. Both consistent with the house style.

CONDITIONS, both already stated and neither new:
  1. tools/reference-scope.sh gains the THIRD JVM-only exception, or it emits `providerParserJVM`
     and reproduces a red gate with zero totals. Your candidate or my follow-up, your call.
  2. Sequence LAST of the three in flight. bb204e9 changes build.sbt, so the moment it lands every
     other pending base becomes influencing under rule 3. NFRD 337600b and scout's 7ee4872 are
     file-disjoint from it and from each other -- I verified zero pairwise overlap -- so landing
     those two first costs nobody a rebase, and landing yours first would cost both of them one.

Your HOLD repairs read well from the checkpoint -- length-prefixed identity parts so provider-node
controls cannot inject boundaries, structural canonical ordering instead of human render, four
restored mutations each naming the court it fails. Formal review is grok's, not mine, and this
ruling does not pre-empt it.
